principles: Reuse only command-local bindings, never global mutable cache state.
Fail closed for real material drift and expose advisory-only reductions explicitly.
Keep the change narrow to DONE and review assurance correctness paths.
drivers: Repeated whole-tree material/story hash recomputation causes workflow cost and risk during DONE/review gates.
Proofbound must remain host-neutral and consumer-neutral; Codex or Claude adapters cannot own workflow evidence.
The implementation must prove stale evidence is still rejected under HEAD, material, and story-owned drift.

options.name: A: command-local hash snapshot contract
pros: Removes duplicate recomputation within a single gate path without retaining state across commands.
Can thread existing materialHash/storyFilesHash args into review escalation and assurance consumers.
Keeps stale detection tied to current git state and material dirty checks.
cons: Requires touching several consumers to pass the snapshot consistently.
Does not solve all possible performance costs across separate CLI invocations.

options.name: B: global persistent materialHash cache
pros: Could reduce repeated recomputation across many commands.
May offer larger speedups for large repositories.
cons: Creates cache invalidation risk around git state, metadata roots, and material exclusions.
Would be optimization-first and outside the approved M1 scope.

options.name: C: no code change, document the pattern only
cons: Does not fix the real repeated recomputation path.
Leaves DONE/review assurance inconsistency in place.

rationale: Choose the narrow command-local snapshot because it addresses the real DONE/review gate pain without introducing a persistent cache or weakening stale evidence checks.

preMortem.trigger: A material file changes after capture but before a consumer evaluates freshness
preMortem.consequence: A stale review or DONE evidence record could be accepted
preMortem.mitigation: Snapshot reuse must require same HEAD and no material dirty files; tests must prove dirty/story drift is rejected.

preMortem.trigger: Implementation starts caching across commands or adding recovery-runner/parallel changes
preMortem.consequence: Story becomes an arbitrary optimization bundle
preMortem.mitigation: Scope boundary excludes global cache, fault injection, streaming rewrite, and parallel execution; review enforces touched files.

preMortem.trigger: One consumer uses supplied snapshot while another recomputes independently
preMortem.consequence: DONE diagnostics disagree and users chase stale commands
preMortem.mitigation: Thread the same binding into DONE oracle review escalation and review assurance floor, and add smoke coverage.
